newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes firm late on moderate short covering.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes firm late on moderate short covering.

text.p: U.S. crudes nudged slightly higher in moderate activity Monday helped by short covering ahead of Wednesday's deadline for Oct pipeline nominations.
Differentials which drifted lower early afternoon, revived as refiners covered last minute requirements.
"People waited for the Iraq thing to settle, but they are starting to talk some term business," a Houston oil broker said, noting interest in West Texas Intermediate Posting Plus.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was at $23.75-90 a barrel, up 22 cents from Friday. The Oct/Nov roll fluctuated between 38 and 50 cents over the session.
Overall wet activity was thinned by the Jewish holiday Yom Kippur, and also by the volatility in the roll.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St James traded from minus 15 cents to 21 cents, but rebounded late in the session.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus moved between postings plus $2.05 and $2.13, later standing around $2.08/2.12.
Demand for heavy, sours was scarce with Eugene Island and West Texas Sour/Midland holding around unchanged.
Outright crude prices reversed earlier losses, with Nov bouncing off support at $22.85 a barrel aided by a resurgence in heating oil futures.
But traders were doubtful if a dearth of heating oil stocks would continue to maintain high refinery runs.
